question.problem: Let $c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c.$

current_example.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-3,5 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-4,0 \rangle$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 5+(-3)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{17}{41}⟨5,-4,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{85}{41},-\frac{68}{41},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
